questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Really easy. The sending institution provided news letters via email and all the needed information was also easily available on their website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As mentioned monthly newsletters were provided both before and during the exchange. The first week of exchange included an orientation week where I met other exchange students, local student tutors, I could get my documents signed, I received a card so I could use public transportation at a discounted rate. I could get my question about course registrations answered.

questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was easy enough. It is part of the application process to the host university. You are asked to choose between to providers (Unihome and Hoas) and whether or not you want to live alone or with flatmates. I lived in a shared Hoas apartment and liked it a lot. Most of my friends lived at Unihome. Unihome has one location for exchange students where as Hoas seems to have several locations. Unihome is more expensive and further away from the city center than most Hoas buildings. Unihome is close to the Viikki campus. Unless you are studying at Viikki campus, I would recommend you choose Hoas instead of Unihome.

You are only offered one accommodation through your University of Helsinki application and it is not necessarily the provider (Hoas or Unihome) that you chose when you applied. There are some private student housing providers that you can find on your own. E.g. Antti Korppi Student House which had several empty places in the spring semester. They are cheaper than the Unihome private apartments.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are no on campus housing. It is very similar to the experience in Copenhagen.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I received an email with a link and information about what I needed to do. I then registered through their website. I needed to register for an IT user account before having access to the online portals. I recommend that you register to everything as soon as you can as some of the processing has a bit of a wait time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were plenty of online guides. I had information in the news letters from the University of Helsinki. I could also email any questions I had.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted-

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
You can't sign up for any classes before your study right begins. The rules for signing up for classes and dropping classes is also a lot more relaxed than that at University of Copenhagen. So don't stress about it. You can sign up for more classes than you need and the try them out for a week or two and then drop the classes you don't want. 

The prerequisites stated in the course unit are not so strict. If you are in doubt about whether or not you have the required knowledge to complete a course, contact the teacher of the course. The teachers are really relaxed and more often than not will let you take a course even if you don't have the necessary prerequisites.

questions.answer: MA

questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took one BA course and five MA courses. Overall I would say that the academic level was slightly lower compared to UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Very similar though the exercise sessions were a little less frequent compared to UCPH.

The workload and exam types varies a lot from course to course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Basic Course in Hydrology, Polar oceans and ice, Stratospheric Dynamics and Chemistry, Arctic climate change, Numerical Meteorology I, Geophysics of Snow and Ice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: For student interested in geophysics, I would recommend Geophysics of Snow and Ice. We went on a 2 day field trip where we gained practical skills in measuring snow properties and drilling ice samples from lake ice.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on holidays to Lapland during the winter. Go on daytrips to Porvoo, Tallinn, Turku, Nuuksio National Park. Visit Hanko and Åland if you have the time.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, it's very similar to Denmark. Most signs, info on foods etc. is also written in Swedish so as a Danish speaking person it's easy to figure everything out.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people in your classes. Like Danish people, Finns are very nice and friendly but most people will not be the ones to initiate the conversation.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There weren't any really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The closeness with nature. How easy it is to just get out of the city and go for a hike.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't stress about signing up for the courses. The rules and deadlines around courses are a lot more relaxed than at UCPH. And you can drop courses easily so consider signing up for more courses than you actually need to take, try them out for a week or two and then drop the ones you don't want.

Ask your teachers if you are ever in doubt about whether or not you can take a course. They are usually pretty easygoing and friendly. The prerequisites in the course descriptions seems more strict than they actually are. Also the teachers can move exams, teaching schedules and assignments as they want to. I was allowed to take the exam in one course another day because I had a field trip in another course.

Enjoy Finland and take lots of trips around the country. I would especially recommend going on one of the student organised trips to Lapland.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Unihome has one location for exchange students where as Hoas seems to have several locations. Unihome is more expensive and further away from the city center than most Hoas buildings. Unihome is close to the Viikki campus. Unless you are studying at Viikki campus, I would recommend you choose Hoas instead of Unihome.

You are only offered one accommodation through your University of Helsinki application and it is not necessarily the provider (Hoas or Unihome) that you chose when you applied. There are some private student housing providers that you can find on your own. E.g. Antti Korppi Student House which had several empty places in the spring semester. They are cheaper than the Unihome private apartments.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I have met and the field trip I went on in the course Geophysics of Snow and Ice.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The periods (what corresponds to the blocks at the Faculty of Science at UCPH) are short (1-2 weeks shorter than at UCPH) so the academic period feels intense and stressfull as the exams are always nearby.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go on an exchange. It is worth it in every way.

questions.answer: Yes
